expressions.context_review_note: Source says never made national news at that stage; preserve negation.

expressions.definition: forcing people to leave a place or group
expressions.example: The manager said they were not kicking people out.
expressions.example_cn: 经理说，他们并没有要把人赶出去。
expressions.source_excerpt: We're not kicking people out, but we're just going to investigate and you guys lose your privileges of throwing fucking ragers and doing keg stands.
expressions.context_review_note: Not literally kicking; source imagined response distinguishes investigation from eviction.

expressions.definition: a brief additional comment outside the main story
expressions.example: A quick side note: the entrance is at the back.
expressions.example_cn: 补充说明一下：入口在后面。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now, side note, house moms of sororities are not like your big sisters, which is like you have a big and you have a little and...
expressions.context_review_note: Signals a digression explaining roles rather than a new event in the timeline.

expressions.definition: an informal name for a residential house director
expressions.cn: 会所宿舍主管（非正式称呼）
expressions.example: The students spoke to the house mom about repairs.
expressions.example_cn: 学生们向宿舍主管反映了维修问题。
expressions.source_excerpt: Then at 8.30 p.m., she states in her lawsuit that she gets into an Uber with her house mom, Jade.
expressions.context_review_note: Not a biological mother or student big sister; role explained in adjacent paragraphs.

expressions.definition: leaves or starts going somewhere
expressions.example: She heads out at eight each morning.
expressions.example_cn: 她每天早上八点出门。
expressions.source_excerpt: She's here for about an hour before she heads out and starts walking back to campus.
expressions.context_review_note: Head is a movement verb here, not a body part.

expressions.definition: allowed Jane to enter; let someone in is the reusable form
expressions.cn: 让简进来；允许某人进入
expressions.example: Please let the visitors in.
expressions.example_cn: 请让访客们进来。
expressions.source_excerpt: They let Jane in and she spots her friend Matthew, right?
expressions.context_review_note: Person-specific source phrase retained; teaching model generalizes the object without presenting it as original dialogue.

expressions.definition: enjoying oneself
expressions.example: The children were having a good time at the picnic.
expressions.example_cn: 孩子们在野餐时玩得很开心。
expressions.source_excerpt: Everybody's having a good time.
expressions.context_review_note: General narrator description of the party; not evidence of any individual's later consent.

expressions.definition: sleep for a short time
expressions.example: I might take a nap after lunch.
expressions.example_cn: 午饭后我可能会小睡一会儿。
expressions.source_excerpt: So he tells Jane Doe that he's going to take a nap.
expressions.context_review_note: Source reports the statement; new example is ordinary daily life.

expressions.definition: moving his hand away from oneself; push something away is the transferable pattern
expressions.example: She kept pushing the loose cable away from her chair.
expressions.example_cn: 她不断把松垂的电缆从椅子旁推开。
expressions.source_excerpt: And she's swatting and like pushing his hand away.
expressions.context_review_note: Source describes resistance; do not recast it as consent or ordinary mutual play.

expressions.definition: a shared messaging conversation with several participants
expressions.example: We use a group chat to arrange meetings.
expressions.example_cn: 我们用群聊安排会议。
expressions.source_excerpt: So it's called like a Xi actives, which means all of the active fraternity members at Chi Phi at Cornell are in this group chat.
expressions.context_review_note: Membership does not prove each person read or acted on a message.

expressions.definition: understand or mentally accept something difficult or surprising
expressions.example: I can't wrap my mind around how quickly things changed.
expressions.example_cn: 我实在想不明白，事情怎么会变化得这么快。
expressions.source_excerpt: This is not even something that happens in fraternity group chats that I can even wrap my mind around.
expressions.context_review_note: Idiomatic mental understanding, not physically wrapping something; mind and head are common variants.

expressions.definition: left suddenly and unexpectedly
expressions.example: He just up and left before the meeting ended.
expressions.example_cn: 会议还没结束，他突然就走了。
expressions.source_excerpt: He just like Diego just like up and left.
expressions.context_review_note: Informal up and + past-tense verb adds suddenness; up is not a separate upward movement.

expressions.definition: bring their phones into use to look at something
expressions.example: They pulled up their phones to check the address.
expressions.example_cn: 他们拿出手机查看地址。
expressions.source_excerpt: They pull up their phones and they're like, oh, my God, the Snapchat, like what's going on?
expressions.context_review_note: Spontaneous source wording; pull up a message on a phone is a more usual way to describe displaying content. Not pull up meaning arrive.

expressions.definition: take something out very quickly; what it refers to depends on context
expressions.cn: 迅速拿出某物（具体所指取决于语境）
expressions.example: When I asked for the receipt, she whipped it out of her bag.
expressions.example_cn: 我问起收据时，她迅速从包里拿了出来。
expressions.source_excerpt: Like you can walk in and whip it out.
expressions.context_review_note: In this quoted message it refers crudely to exposing a penis, not to an ordinary object. The teaching example deliberately uses a neutral object and is not a podcast quotation.

expressions.definition: did not know at all
expressions.example: I had no clue the meeting had been moved.
expressions.example_cn: 我完全不知道会议改了时间。
expressions.source_excerpt: It's not like an illegal picture in the sense that she was unclothed or engaged in activity that she did not consent to being filmed but it is a picture of her that she had no clue was taken
expressions.context_review_note: Source uses it about a picture being taken without her knowledge; not knowing about the picture is distinct from the narrator's legal characterization.

expressions.definition: at all, used to emphasize a negative statement
expressions.example: I have no doubt whatsoever.
expressions.example_cn: 我丝毫不怀疑。
expressions.source_excerpt: I have no recollection of that whatsoever.
expressions.context_review_note: Emphasizes no recollection; not a question word despite beginning with what.

expressions.definition: someone within an organization who provides information
expressions.cn: 内部消息来源；知情人士
expressions.example: The report cited an inside source.
expressions.example_cn: 报道援引了一位内部知情人士。
expressions.source_excerpt: But I think they got it from an inside source or something of that matter, and they've been releasing random snippets every single day, just like, here's another random line.
expressions.context_review_note: I think marks speculation about the source, not confirmed provenance.

expressions.definition: assembled separate pieces of information into an account
expressions.example: We pieced together the timeline from old emails.
expressions.example_cn: 我们根据旧邮件拼出了时间线。
expressions.source_excerpt: So it's like a hundred page lawsuit and there's just a lot of, a lot of information in there that we've pieced together and tried to cross.
expressions.context_review_note: Information-reconstruction sense; the trailing tried to cross is incomplete and remains flagged.

expressions.definition: information that is widely known rather than private
expressions.cn: 众所周知的事；公开的信息
expressions.example: The decision is now public knowledge.
expressions.example_cn: 这项决定现在已经公开了。
expressions.source_excerpt: And it's not until later that day, she starts becoming aware of what exactly happened to her at the frat house the night before and how this is all, like it's all becoming public knowledge.
expressions.context_review_note: The account describes information becoming widely known, not proof that every circulated claim is accurate.

expressions.definition: respond successfully to a difficult situation
expressions.example: The team will rise to this challenge.
expressions.example_cn: 团队会迎接并应对这一挑战。
expressions.source_excerpt: I am confident that our community will rise to this challenge as it has to others and continue to pursue our individual and collective goals throughout the academic year.
expressions.context_review_note: Formal motivational language in the quoted statement, not a claim that the challenge has already been resolved.

expressions.definition: examining something very carefully to find information
expressions.example: We spent the morning combing through old records.
expressions.example_cn: 我们花了一上午仔细查阅旧记录。
expressions.source_excerpt: The general public is also very busy with Thanksgiving festivities, and I highly doubt news reporters and journalists are combing through Cornell's official statement websites to look for any suspicious activity.
expressions.context_review_note: Figurative combing, not grooming hair; the narrator doubts reporters were doing this.

expressions.definition: organized or assembled something from people or parts
expressions.example: They put together a team for the project.
expressions.example_cn: 他们为这个项目组建了一个团队。
expressions.source_excerpt: And they put together this panel.
expressions.context_review_note: Panel is an assembled group, not a physical board being constructed.

expressions.definition: seek to have a criminal accusation formally pursued
expressions.cn: 要求追究刑事责任；提出刑事控告（通俗说法）
expressions.example: The article discusses whether anyone sought to press charges.
expressions.example_cn: 文章讨论是否有人要求追究刑事责任。
expressions.source_excerpt: They cannot press charges.
expressions.context_review_note: Ordinary-language expression, not a claim that a private individual controls prosecution; surrounding claims about authority remain attributed and require legal-context review.

expressions.definition: becoming more active or intense
expressions.example: By noon, the wind was really kicking up.
expressions.example_cn: 到中午时，风明显大了起来。
expressions.source_excerpt: It's really in May of 2025 that things start really kicking up.
expressions.context_review_note: Informal activity/intensity sense; source things start really kicking up is less specific than starting a formal proceeding.

expressions.definition: is taken up and reported by media organizations
expressions.example: The local story gets picked up by a national newspaper.
expressions.example_cn: 这则地方新闻被一家全国性报纸跟进报道。
expressions.source_excerpt: And this case gets picked up instantly after Jane Doe's lawsuit by almost every single mainstream media news outlet in the United States.
expressions.context_review_note: News uptake, not physical lifting, collection by car or arrest.

expressions.definition: suddenly attracts a great deal of attention
expressions.cn: 迅速引发广泛关注；爆火
expressions.example: The video blows up after a popular account shares it.
expressions.example_cn: 一个热门账号转发后，这段视频迅速引发广泛关注。
expressions.source_excerpt: Celebrities start posting pictures of the Cornell 7 and it completely blows up.
expressions.context_review_note: Figurative spread of attention, not an explosion or an angry outburst.

expressions.definition: immediately after a particular event or condition
expressions.example: I'll send the file as soon as I finish editing it.
expressions.example_cn: 我一编辑完就把文件发给你。
expressions.source_excerpt: That's going to come up as soon as I can edit and I will see you in the next one.
expressions.context_review_note: Source ties the next release to finishing the edit, not a promised date or fabricated timestamp.

expressions.definition: becomes a subject of news reporting
expressions.cn: 成为新闻；登上新闻报道
expressions.example: A small community project rarely makes the news.
expressions.example_cn: 一个小型社区项目很少登上新闻。
expressions.source_excerpt: But the reason that this makes the news is because, well, like I said, it's Cornell University and it's such a strange, bizarre incident with a strange conclusion.
expressions.context_review_note: Make the news is not manufacture news. Here it introduces why the incident attracted attention, not a claim about the accuracy of coverage.

expressions.definition: an unusual or puzzling outcome or judgment
expressions.example: The report reaches a strange conclusion from very little evidence.
expressions.example_cn: 报告仅凭很少的证据就得出了一个奇怪的结论。
expressions.source_excerpt: But the reason that this makes the news is because, well, like I said, it's Cornell University and it's such a strange, bizarre incident with a strange conclusion.
expressions.context_review_note: Ordinary adjective–noun combination; conclusion can mean outcome or judgment. The preceding account makes the narrator's puzzlement about responsibility salient.

expressions.definition: despite what has just been said
expressions.example: The route was longer; nevertheless, we arrived on time.
expressions.example_cn: 路线更长了，尽管如此，我们还是按时到达。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now, nevertheless, as the president introduces the debate series, he's now leaving the atrium.
expressions.context_review_note: Contrastive discourse adverb often used in formal speech and writing. In this transition it does not supply missing evidence about the event.

expressions.definition: recorded moving images of an event
expressions.example: We reviewed the security footage after the alarm.
expressions.example_cn: 警报响起后，我们查看了监控录像。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now from the footage that I saw that's been released, it doesn't look like the students are jumping up on his car.
expressions.context_review_note: Uncountable in this sense: some footage or a piece of footage, not a footage. The narrator has seen released material, not necessarily all recordings.

expressions.definition: been made available for people to see or use
expressions.example: The updated instructions have been released.
expressions.example_cn: 更新后的说明已经发布了。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now from the footage that I saw that's been released, it doesn't look like the students are jumping up on his car.
expressions.context_review_note: Been released forms a perfect passive after has/have. In that's been released, that's means that has, and that refers to the footage.

expressions.definition: move backward out of a space, especially in a vehicle
expressions.example: She carefully backed out of the garage.
expressions.example_cn: 她小心地把车倒出了车库。
expressions.source_excerpt: And it's very clear there's one student standing behind his car so that he can't back out of the parking spot.
expressions.context_review_note: Physical movement in back out of the parking spot; distinguish the figurative back out of a deal, meaning withdraw from an agreement.

expressions.definition: with the result or purpose that something happens
expressions.example: I moved the lamp so that I could read more easily.
expressions.example_cn: 我挪了挪灯，以便看书更方便。
expressions.source_excerpt: And it's very clear there's one student standing behind his car so that he can't back out of the parking spot.
expressions.context_review_note: Links the person's position to the car's inability to back out. The connector can express purpose or result; source phrasing alone cannot prove intention.

expressions.definition: a vehicle system designed to apply the brakes automatically under specified conditions
expressions.example: The manual explains the automatic braking system's limitations.
expressions.example_cn: 手册说明了自动制动系统的局限。
expressions.source_excerpt: An automatic braking system was able to slowly maneuver my car from the parking space and exit the parking lot.
expressions.context_review_note: Technical noun phrase, not a synonym for self-driving. The quoted claim about maneuvering remains the speaker's account and is not verified as a vehicle capability.

expressions.definition: preventing someone from expressing views
expressions.cn: 压制言论；阻止他人发声
expressions.example: They argued that the rule risked silencing speech.
expressions.example_cn: 他们认为，这条规定可能会压制言论。
expressions.source_excerpt: It is harassment and intimidation with the direct motive of silencing speech.
expressions.context_review_note: Silence is a verb meaning suppress expression, not merely reduce volume. Motive is alleged by the quoted speaker, not established by this vocabulary entry.

expressions.definition: as an assumed consequence when no separate choice or distinction is made
expressions.example: By default, new files are saved in this folder.
expressions.example_cn: 默认情况下，新文件保存在这个文件夹里。
expressions.source_excerpt: For Cornell and by default, Michael Kotlikoff, the president, has now deemed that it's the student's fault and he can't come back to campus for a full year.
expressions.context_review_note: Default is literal system behavior in the teaching example; source uses it loosely to extend responsibility from the university to its president. That is the narrator's inference, not a legal rule.

expressions.definition: opposing someone or taking a contrary position
expressions.example: Several team members were going against the proposal.
expressions.example_cn: 几位团队成员反对这个提案。
expressions.source_excerpt: There are people in mainstream media who are going on talk shows like The View going against Jane Doe, Trump.
expressions.context_review_note: Opposition sense, not physical travel against a direction. The source does not establish whether criticism is justified.

expressions.definition: apparently, though not known for certain
expressions.example: A seemingly simple task took the whole afternoon.
expressions.example_cn: 一项看似简单的任务花了整个下午。
expressions.source_excerpt: There are Snapchat messages that are being analyzed, new text messages seemingly released like every single day,
expressions.context_review_note: Signals appearance rather than certainty. Source's seemingly released describes the narrator's impression of the stream of messages.

expressions.definition: undergoing careful examination
expressions.cn: 正在被分析或仔细研究
expressions.example: The survey responses are being analyzed.
expressions.example_cn: 调查回复正在被分析。
expressions.source_excerpt: There are Snapchat messages that are being analyzed, new text messages seemingly released like every single day,
expressions.context_review_note: Present-progressive passive: are being + past participle. It describes an ongoing process without naming the analysts or proving the conclusions.

expressions.definition: all day, every day
expressions.cn: 全天候；每周七天、每天二十四小时
expressions.example: The automated help page is available 24-7.
expressions.example_cn: 自动帮助页面全天候开放。
expressions.source_excerpt: Of sexual violence available 24-7 by phone chat or text
expressions.context_review_note: Read twenty-four seven. This availability label does not reconstruct the missing subject in the source fragment or verify any organization's service hours.

expressions.definition: written references and supporting information accompanying a podcast episode
expressions.cn: 播客节目附注；本期参考资料
expressions.example: The links are listed in the show notes.
expressions.example_cn: 链接列在本期节目附注中。
expressions.source_excerpt: As always, full show notes are available at rottenmangopodcast.com.
expressions.context_review_note: Podcast sense, not notes for a theatrical performance. Source identifies where notes can be found; this card does not verify the website's current contents.

expressions.definition: a notice that upcoming material may be distressing
expressions.cn: 内容预警；敏感内容提示
expressions.example: The episode begins with a content warning.
expressions.example_cn: 这一集开头有一则内容预警。
expressions.source_excerpt: Before we begin a big content warning,
expressions.context_review_note: A notice before difficult material, not a claim that everyone will react the same way. Source fragment introduces the next paragraph's topics.

expressions.definition: documents formally submitted to a court
expressions.cn: 提交法院的文书；诉讼文件
expressions.example: The article quotes several court filings.
expressions.example_cn: 文章引用了几份提交法院的文书。
expressions.source_excerpt: When we describe what happened that night, we're describing what is alleged in court filings, reported by news outlets, or found in public records up until the time of recording.
expressions.context_review_note: A filing can contain a party's allegations; inclusion in a court document does not by itself establish that every statement is a judicial finding.

expressions.definition: official records available for public access
expressions.cn: 公开记录；可公开查阅的官方档案
expressions.example: The team checked public records before publishing the story.
expressions.example_cn: 团队在发布报道前查阅了公开档案。
expressions.source_excerpt: When we describe what happened that night, we're describing what is alleged in court filings, reported by news outlets, or found in public records up until the time of recording.
expressions.context_review_note: A source category distinct from a news report or a party's claims. Availability and access conditions vary; the phrase alone does not guarantee unrestricted access.

expressions.definition: a description that makes something seem larger or stronger than it really is
expressions.example: Calling it a disaster was an exaggeration.
expressions.example_cn: 把它称为灾难有些夸张了。
expressions.source_excerpt: Obviously an exaggeration, but it just feels like that.
expressions.context_review_note: The narrator explicitly retracts a literal headcount reading of the football-team comparison; a rhetorical quantity is not a measured number.

expressions.definition: a humorously large group, compared to a sports team
expressions.cn: 足有一整支美式橄榄球队那么多的……（夸张说法）
expressions.example: We seem to need a whole football team of people to move this sofa.
expressions.example_cn: 搬这张沙发，感觉简直要一整支美式橄榄球队那么多人。
expressions.source_excerpt: And I will say there is like a whole football team of lawyers involved.
expressions.context_review_note: Creative exaggeration, not a fixed numerical unit or standard team-size claim. Segment 142 explicitly confirms that the narrator is exaggerating.

expressions.definition: sent or delivered through the postal service
expressions.example: Your replacement card is in the mail.
expressions.example_cn: 你的补办卡已经寄出了。
expressions.source_excerpt: They'll ship you one of those like plastic insurance cards in the mail that means absolutely nothing at this point.
expressions.context_review_note: Mail here is physical post, not email. Ship you a card means send a card to you, without implying transport by sea.

expressions.definition: has no significance or practical value in the stated situation
expressions.cn: 毫无意义；没有任何实际价值
expressions.example: A promise means absolutely nothing without follow-through.
expressions.example_cn: 没有后续行动，承诺就毫无意义。
expressions.source_excerpt: They'll ship you one of those like plastic insurance cards in the mail that means absolutely nothing at this point.
expressions.context_review_note: Emphatic evaluation, not proof that an insurance card has no legal or practical use. Source expresses the narrator's critical opinion.

expressions.definition: women's college social organizations, especially in the United States
expressions.example: Several sororities took part in the campus event.
expressions.example_cn: 几个姐妹会参加了校园活动。
expressions.source_excerpt: Some people say it's fraternities and sororities.
expressions.context_review_note: Organization sense, not biological sisters. Compare fraternities; membership practices and particular organizations should not be inferred from this generic term.

expressions.definition: the fraternity and sorority system at a U.S. college
expressions.cn: 美国大学的兄弟会与姐妹会体系及其活动
expressions.example: The guide explains Greek life on campus.
expressions.example_cn: 指南介绍了校园里的兄弟会与姐妹会体系。
expressions.source_excerpt: It's all Greek life.
expressions.context_review_note: Greek refers to organizations' Greek-letter names, not everyday life in Greece. Clarifies the extension from fraternities to both kinds of organizations.

expressions.definition: probably removed from membership or an arrangement
expressions.cn: 很可能被取消资格或除名
expressions.example: Members who stop renewing are likely dropped from the mailing list.
expressions.example_cn: 不再续订的成员很可能会被移出邮件名单。
expressions.source_excerpt: All of that, the second that there's a court filing, that member is likely dropped.
expressions.context_review_note: Dropped is an informal removal sense, not physically released. Source refers to membership and says likely, not an automatic verified rule.

expressions.definition: a strip worn around part of the body, here apparently the wrist
expressions.example: Each guest wore a band around their wrist.
expressions.example_cn: 每位来宾手腕上都戴着一条带子。
expressions.source_excerpt: And then you get a band that you can't take off and you can only drink your own beer.
expressions.context_review_note: Entry-control context suggests a wristband, but the PDF says band; keep that inference explicit and do not replace the quoted noun.

expressions.definition: other members of the same fraternity
expressions.cn: 同一兄弟会的其他成员
expressions.example: He planned the event with his fellow fraternity brothers.
expressions.example_cn: 他与同一兄弟会的其他成员一起策划了活动。
expressions.source_excerpt: But like the people that are checking all these things are your fellow fraternity brothers that are also 18, 19, probably maybe 21.
expressions.context_review_note: Fellow means sharing membership, not a male stranger, and brothers is organizational rather than biological kinship.

expressions.definition: people who are not members of the fraternity in this context
expressions.example: The event was open to non-brothers as well.
expressions.example_cn: 那项活动也向非本会成员开放。
expressions.source_excerpt: We technically could not throw a football around in the front yard with non-brothers that were there because according to the policy, anything athletic was too much of a liability for the insurance company.
expressions.context_review_note: Contextual non- prefix negates membership, not a biological family relationship; term is informal and organization-specific.

expressions.definition: involving sports or physical exercise
expressions.example: The school offers several athletic activities.
expressions.example_cn: 学校提供几种体育活动。
expressions.source_excerpt: We technically could not throw a football around in the front yard with non-brothers that were there because according to the policy, anything athletic was too much of a liability for the insurance company.
expressions.context_review_note: Anything athletic means activities involving sports here, not only people with a fit body. Does not validate the quoted insurance restriction.

expressions.definition: equal in rank or score to another item
expressions.example: The team was tied with its rival for fifth place.
expressions.example_cn: 这支队伍与对手并列第五。
expressions.source_excerpt: The fourth is fall from heights and the fifth is auto accidents and tied with fifth is at just 7% hazing incidents.
expressions.context_review_note: Tied is equal rank here, not physically bound. Source's tied with fifth is compressed speech for sharing fifth place.

expressions.definition: accidents involving motor vehicles
expressions.example: The report lists auto accidents as a separate category.
expressions.example_cn: 报告把机动车事故列为单独一类。
expressions.source_excerpt: The fourth is fall from heights and the fifth is auto accidents and tied with fifth is at just 7% hazing incidents.
expressions.context_review_note: Auto is an American shortening of automobile, not automatic. Source's percentage belongs to the cited comparison, not a general rate for all students.

expressions.definition: the supposedly less serious end of a range in this context
expressions.cn: 相对较轻的一面（这里是说话者的归类）
expressions.example: He called the delay 'the light side' of their problems, but I disagreed.
expressions.example_cn: 他把延期称为他们那些问题中“比较轻的一面”，但我不同意。
expressions.source_excerpt: And that's usually like the light side of hazing.
expressions.context_review_note: Not illumination or automatically a humorous side. Source minimizes some harmful conduct relative to worse acts; the wording does not make that conduct safe or acceptable.

expressions.definition: complete, intense or outright, informally
expressions.example: A small disagreement became a full-on argument.
expressions.example_cn: 一个小分歧变成了一场激烈争吵。
expressions.source_excerpt: There is the full-on sexual assault side of hazing as well.
expressions.context_review_note: Informal intensifier before a noun or adjective. In source it contrasts a purportedly lighter category with outright sexual assault; not a safety distinction.

expressions.definition: a bed arrangement with one bed above another
expressions.example: The small room has a bunk bed and a desk.
expressions.example_cn: 这个小房间里有一张上下铺床和一张书桌。
expressions.source_excerpt: Sometimes there will be a bunk bed next to an open window and they'll be intoxicated, roll out of the bed and then roll out the window, fall from fire escapes, fall from balconies.
expressions.context_review_note: Compound names stacked sleeping spaces. Source lists separate dangerous fall situations; do not infer a single uninterrupted sequence.

expressions.definition: a small shallow pool of water on a surface
expressions.example: There was a puddle of water near the doorway.
expressions.example_cn: 门口附近有一小摊积水。
expressions.source_excerpt: But also if someone walks into the building and they slip on a puddle of water, they might sue the school.
expressions.context_review_note: Puddle is small and shallow, not a pond. The source says might sue, which is a possible legal action rather than established liability.

expressions.definition: tells the details of a past event or experience
expressions.example: The article recounts her first year at work.
expressions.example_cn: 文章讲述了她工作的第一年。
expressions.source_excerpt: And he recounts his hazing experience.
expressions.context_review_note: Reporting verb, not recalculating a number. Recounting an experience attributes an account rather than independently proving each detail.

expressions.definition: fully developed or having complete membership or status
expressions.cn: 完全成熟的；具备正式资格的
expressions.example: The prototype became a fully fledged product.
expressions.example_cn: 原型变成了一个成熟的产品。
expressions.source_excerpt: Fully fledged, fully pledged Chi Phi member if they can just endure the next few hours.
expressions.context_review_note: Usually fully fledged before a noun; source then says fully pledged, a correction or wordplay tied to fraternity pledging. Preserve both original forms.

expressions.definition: was made up of the listed components
expressions.example: The presentation consisted of three short sections.
expressions.example_cn: 演示由三个简短部分组成。
expressions.source_excerpt: He says mung consisted of cold oatmeal, vinegar, hot sauce, and cayenne pepper.
expressions.context_review_note: Consist of is not normally passive: consisted of, not was consisted of. Teaching example avoids turning the abusive mixture description into a recipe.

expressions.definition: forced to move on hands and knees or with the body close to the ground
expressions.example: The novel describes people being made to crawl through a narrow passage.
expressions.example_cn: 小说描写了人们被迫爬过一条狭窄通道。
expressions.source_excerpt: Then i was blindfolded again made to crawl on my elbows and knees on hard wooden floors
expressions.context_review_note: Passive made to + verb expresses compulsion; active make someone crawl has no to. Source's missing was is retained, not silently repaired in the quotation.

expressions.definition: fell down suddenly because the body could no longer stay upright
expressions.example: The exhausted character collapsed beside the door.
expressions.example_cn: 那个筋疲力尽的角色倒在门旁。
expressions.source_excerpt: Finally, I collapsed.
expressions.context_review_note: Physical sense in source, not a company failing or a menu closing. No medical cause or diagnosis is inferred.

expressions.definition: an entire article or written account in this context
expressions.example: There's a whole piece about the project in the local paper.
expressions.example_cn: 当地报纸有一整篇文章介绍这个项目。
expressions.source_excerpt: There's a whole piece on this that Jared shares in the Cornell Sun, which was published recently.
expressions.context_review_note: Piece is a written work, not a physical fragment. Cornell Sun is the named publication, and recently is recording-relative.

expressions.definition: bottles containing or previously containing distilled alcoholic drinks
expressions.example: The recycling bin contained empty liquor bottles.
expressions.example_cn: 回收箱里有空的烈酒瓶。
expressions.source_excerpt: There's beer cans, liquor bottles.
expressions.context_review_note: American liquor usually means spirits, distinct from beer and wine. Presence of bottles alone does not prove who drank their contents.

expressions.definition: very soon, in informal speech
expressions.example: I'll explain the changes in a second.
expressions.example_cn: 我马上解释这些改动。
expressions.source_excerpt: When you go through little snippets of the Title IX investigation, which is the Jane Doe investigation that we're going to kind of get into in a second, there are allegations that someone overdosed.
expressions.context_review_note: Usually not literally one second. In the source get into means discuss, and the phrase previews the topic rather than specifying an audio timestamp.

expressions.definition: not permitted or not expected to do something under a rule or norm
expressions.example: You're not supposed to leave boxes in the hallway.
expressions.example_cn: 按规定，你不应该把箱子放在走廊里。
expressions.source_excerpt: Because it's like, hey, you're not supposed to have drugs on campus.
expressions.context_review_note: Rule/expectation, not physical inability. Source is a paraphrased institutional reaction, not a complete statement of drug law.

expressions.text: whether on the road or in the chapter house
expressions.definition: in either of the two settings named
expressions.cn: 无论在外途中还是在分会会所里
expressions.example: Whether on the road or at home, she keeps in touch with friends.
expressions.example_cn: 无论在旅途中还是在家，她都和朋友保持联系。
expressions.source_excerpt: They have a creed of Kai-Fai and it reads in short, I believe in the friendship of Kai-Fai, whether on the road or in the chapter house, the hand of brotherhood is always extended.
expressions.context_review_note: Whether A or B covers alternatives. The teaching example changes the second location explicitly; source's hand-of-brotherhood metaphor still needs separate support.

expressions.definition: expected or required to do or be something
expressions.example: The coordinator is supposed to help new members.
expressions.example_cn: 协调员按职责应该帮助新成员。
expressions.source_excerpt: Supposed to kind of be a caretaker.
expressions.context_review_note: Be supposed to + verb; the fragment omits be because it continues the prior description. Indicates expected responsibility, not verified performance.

expressions.definition: press a mark onto a surface using a stamp
expressions.example: Staff stamp each ticket at the entrance.
expressions.example_cn: 工作人员在入口给每张票盖印。
expressions.source_excerpt: They stamp these giant X's on both of Jane's hands.
expressions.context_review_note: Verb of marking here, not a postage-stamp noun or stamping a foot. X's means X-shaped marks; giant is emphatic size description.

expressions.definition: organized around images or ideas associated with Hawaii
expressions.example: The invitation describes a Hawaii-themed event.
expressions.example_cn: 邀请函把活动描述为以夏威夷为主题。
expressions.source_excerpt: The Chi Phi fraternity house is hosting a Hawaii themed party, which is an interesting choice for October 19th, but it's Hawaii themed.
expressions.context_review_note: Use -themed after a theme word and a hyphen in edited prose. The phrase does not verify cultural authenticity or alter the narrated event date.

expressions.definition: having the capacity to give meaningful agreement
expressions.cn: 具备作出有效同意的能力
expressions.example: The training discusses what it means to be capable of consenting.
expressions.example_cn: 培训讨论了具备作出有效同意的能力意味着什么。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now, according to the lawsuit, Jane at this point is so drunk, she's not even capable of consenting to any of this.
expressions.context_review_note: Capable of + -ing; source alleges incapacity in a particular situation. This language note does not make a clinical or legal capacity determination.

expressions.definition: repeatedly supplied or pressed the plaintiff to take something
expressions.cn: 不断向原告提供或劝其接受……
expressions.example: The host plied the visitors with offers of tea.
expressions.example_cn: 主人不断向来访者劝茶。
expressions.source_excerpt: The lawsuit says during this time, defendant Matthew and Jonathan also plied plaintiff with marijuana and quote, Jamaican liquor believed to be some high proof rum.
expressions.context_review_note: Ply someone with something suggests persistent supply or urging. The neutral example teaches the construction without reproducing the alleged substance administration.

expressions.definition: taking part in an activity
expressions.example: The group is engaging in a discussion.
expressions.example_cn: 小组正在参与讨论。
expressions.source_excerpt: Soon after defendant Matthew and Jonathan began engaging in sexual acts with plaintiff all without her consent.
expressions.context_review_note: Formal engage in + activity. Source sexual acts means sexual activity, and all without her consent denies voluntary agreement; engaging in does not itself imply consent.

expressions.definition: extend a hand toward something to try to take or touch it
expressions.example: She reached for the folder on the shelf.
expressions.example_cn: 她伸手去拿架子上的文件夹。
expressions.source_excerpt: Meanwhile, Jonathan keeps, according to the lawsuit, keeps trying to reach for her private parts down there.
expressions.context_review_note: For marks the target of an attempt, not successful contact. Source alleges repeated unwanted attempts, with attribution preserved.

expressions.definition: a polite or indirect term for genital areas
expressions.example: The safety lesson explains the term private parts respectfully.
expressions.example_cn: 安全课程以尊重的方式解释“私处”这个词。
expressions.source_excerpt: Meanwhile, Jonathan keeps, according to the lawsuit, keeps trying to reach for her private parts down there.
expressions.context_review_note: Receptive euphemism, not an ordinary ownership phrase. Source's down there reinforces the same anatomical reference without adding detail.

expressions.definition: making a quick striking movement to hit or brush something away
expressions.example: She was swatting a fly away from the food.
expressions.example_cn: 她正挥手把一只苍蝇从食物旁赶开。
expressions.source_excerpt: And she's swatting and like pushing his hand away.
expressions.context_review_note: Quick striking/warding-off motion, not generic pushing. Source describes resistance to unwanted contact; teaching example uses an insect.

expressions.definition: takes hold of suddenly or firmly
expressions.example: He grabs the rail when the bus stops.
expressions.example_cn: 公交车停下时，他一把抓住扶手。
expressions.source_excerpt: Jane alleges that Jillio just grabs Jane from Jonathan.
expressions.context_review_note: Physical hold, not a rescue motive. Source's grabs Jane from Jonathan indicates a change in who holds her; later narration explicitly undermines the hoped-for rescue interpretation.

expressions.definition: genuine or credible, informally
expressions.example: The offer looks legit, but let's verify the sender.
expressions.example_cn: 这项优惠看起来像真的，不过我们先核实发送者。
expressions.source_excerpt: However, when I'm reading this, I'm reading this as like, no, this must be legit because my buddy just went in there and he, I haven't seen him since.
expressions.context_review_note: Short for legitimate. Source's must be legit is part of the narrator's imagined reading of a message, not authentication.

expressions.definition: very drunk, informally
expressions.example: The novel describes a guest as hammered after the party.
expressions.example_cn: 小说把一位宾客描写为聚会后喝得烂醉。
expressions.source_excerpt: I look hammered in it.
expressions.context_review_note: Informal intoxication adjective, not physically struck with a hammer. Source is a person's interpretation of her appearance in a photograph, not a measured alcohol level.

expressions.definition: started suddenly, especially of unrest, conflict or another disruptive event
expressions.example: An argument broke out during the meeting.
expressions.example_cn: 会议期间突然爆发了一场争论。
expressions.source_excerpt: To give some context, right before this whole parking lot fiasco, Cornell's president, Michael Kotlikoff, had just introduced to Cornell students the Israel-Palestinian debate series, which this comes after a series of protests broke out on campus demanding justice for Palestine and some pretty
expressions.context_review_note: Break out is intransitive here. Source connects protests with the preceding institutional response; grammatical nesting is disfluent but the event relation is identifiable.

expressions.definition: strongly calling for fair treatment or accountability
expressions.example: The group issued a statement demanding justice.
expressions.example_cn: 团体发表声明，呼吁公正处理。
expressions.source_excerpt: To give some context, right before this whole parking lot fiasco, Cornell's president, Michael Kotlikoff, had just introduced to Cornell students the Israel-Palestinian debate series, which this comes after a series of protests broke out on campus demanding justice for Palestine and some pretty
expressions.context_review_note: Demanding is a participle describing protesters' stated aim; not demanding as an adjective meaning difficult. Language review does not decide the political merits of a demand.

expressions.definition: punished very harshly
expressions.cn: 受到严厉或残酷的惩罚
expressions.example: The novel describes a child who was brutally punished.
expressions.example_cn: 小说描写了一个受到残酷惩罚的孩子。
expressions.source_excerpt: After Cornell students felt like they've been brutally punished for peacefully protesting, there's gonna be a lot of emotions involved.
expressions.context_review_note: Brutally is a strong evaluation. Source says students felt like this happened, preserving their perceived experience rather than independently measuring punishment.

expressions.definition: expressing public opposition without violence
expressions.example: The report describes residents peacefully protesting the closure.
expressions.example_cn: 报告描述居民正和平抗议关闭决定。
expressions.source_excerpt: After Cornell students felt like they've been brutally punished for peacefully protesting, there's gonna be a lot of emotions involved.
expressions.context_review_note: Peacefully modifies the manner of protest. Source's contrast with harsh punishment is part of the reported perspective, not this review's factual adjudication.

expressions.definition: feelings connected with or affecting a situation
expressions.example: There are strong emotions involved in this decision.
expressions.example_cn: 这个决定牵涉到强烈的情绪。
expressions.source_excerpt: After Cornell students felt like they've been brutally punished for peacefully protesting, there's gonna be a lot of emotions involved.
expressions.context_review_note: Involved describes feelings present in the situation. Source gonna be is conversational going to be, predicting emotional stakes rather than a physical action.

expressions.definition: recognized or familiar to a person or organization
expressions.example: The issue is known to the support team.
expressions.example_cn: 支持团队已经知道这个问题。
expressions.source_excerpt: The whole situation gets so big that the president of Cornell has to release a public statement where he says, these individuals are known to Cornell for their past conduct, including a long history of ongoing verbal and online abuse towards numerous members of Cornell's administration and staff.
expressions.context_review_note: Known to + knower differs from known for + characteristic. In source the institution claims familiarity with prior conduct; that claim is not independently verified.

expressions.definition: continuing abusive speech and abusive conduct over the internet
expressions.cn: 持续的言语及网络辱骂或侵扰
expressions.example: The report describes ongoing verbal and online abuse directed at staff.
expressions.example_cn: 报告描述了针对员工的持续言语和网络侵扰。
expressions.source_excerpt: The whole situation gets so big that the president of Cornell has to release a public statement where he says, these individuals are known to Cornell for their past conduct, including a long history of ongoing verbal and online abuse towards numerous members of Cornell's administration and staff.
expressions.context_review_note: Ongoing means continuing; abuse here is harmful treatment or speech, not substance abuse. This is the institution's characterization in the quoted statement.

expressions.definition: not acceptable or appropriate within a community or setting
expressions.cn: 在……中不应有容身之地；不被接受
expressions.example: Bullying has no place in our workplace.
expressions.example_cn: 我们的工作场所不容许霸凌。
expressions.source_excerpt: It is no place in an academic community, no place in a democracy and can have no place at Cornell.
expressions.context_review_note: Figurative acceptance, not a lack of physical space. Source opens It is no place, which remains suspect wording and is not copied into the teaching example.

expressions.definition: a student in the final year of a typical U.S. high-school or undergraduate program
expressions.cn: 毕业年级学生；这里指大学四年级学生
expressions.example: She's a senior preparing her final project.
expressions.example_cn: 她是毕业年级学生，正在准备毕业项目。
expressions.source_excerpt: So he was a senior and he graduated.
expressions.context_review_note: Student-year sense, not an elderly person or a high-ranking employee. Source then says graduated, fitting that educational context.

expressions.definition: formally start a noncriminal court action by submitting the required papers
expressions.example: The fictional company plans to file a civil lawsuit over the contract.
expressions.example_cn: 虚构的那家公司计划就合同提起民事诉讼。
expressions.source_excerpt: Because a few months later, Jane Doe will file a civil lawsuit against Cornell University and seven fraternity brothers from Cornell, now dubbed the Cornell Seven.
expressions.context_review_note: Civil action is distinguished from criminal prosecution; filing does not establish liability or mean the plaintiff has won.

expressions.definition: given a name or label, especially by others
expressions.example: The new room was dubbed the quiet corner.
expressions.example_cn: 新房间被称为“安静角”。
expressions.source_excerpt: Because a few months later, Jane Doe will file a civil lawsuit against Cornell University and seven fraternity brothers from Cornell, now dubbed the Cornell Seven.
expressions.context_review_note: Naming sense, not replacing a film's audio. The label Cornell Seven is a name used in the account, not a judgment about each person's conduct.

expressions.definition: a short organized session for discussion, learning or practice
expressions.example: The team attended a workshop on clear communication.
expressions.example_cn: 团队参加了一场关于清晰沟通的工作坊。
expressions.source_excerpt: And some of the accused, their punishment for the events of that night was to attend a workshop and write essays, reflection essays, reflection papers.
expressions.context_review_note: Educational event sense, not a place for repairing machines. Source describes a reported response to alleged conduct without validating its adequacy.

expressions.definition: written pieces in which people examine an experience and what they learned
expressions.example: Students wrote reflection papers after the project.
expressions.example_cn: 项目结束后，学生们写了反思文章。
expressions.source_excerpt: And some of the accused, their punishment for the events of that night was to attend a workshop and write essays, reflection essays, reflection papers.
expressions.context_review_note: Reflection means thoughtful consideration, not a mirror image. Source's essays, reflection essays, reflection papers is a self-correction rather than necessarily three distinct tasks.

expressions.definition: said clearly and directly rather than merely implied
expressions.example: The instructions explicitly stated that copies were acceptable.
expressions.example_cn: 说明明确表示可以使用副本。
expressions.source_excerpt: Jane Doe has also explicitly stated through her lawyer that any donations meant for her should be redirected to RAINN.
expressions.context_review_note: Explicitly concerns clarity of wording, not independent truth. Through her lawyer means via a representative; the reported statement is not newly authenticated.

expressions.definition: sent or directed to a different destination or recipient
expressions.cn: 被转向；被改送至其他对象
expressions.example: The message was redirected to the support team.
expressions.example_cn: 消息被转发给了支持团队。
expressions.source_excerpt: Jane Doe has also explicitly stated through her lawyer that any donations meant for her should be redirected to RAINN.
expressions.context_review_note: Re- adds change of direction here. Source concerns intended donations, not an instruction from this assistant to transfer money.

expressions.definition: enabled an action or result
expressions.example: The shared timetable made it possible to coordinate our visits.
expressions.example_cn: 共享时间表让我们能够协调到访时间。
expressions.source_excerpt: This episode's partnerships have also made it possible to support Rotten Mango's team of dedicated researchers.
expressions.context_review_note: It is a placeholder before the to-infinitive; possible describes feasibility. Not a claim that the result was guaranteed by every partnership.

expressions.definition: cooperative arrangements between people or organizations
expressions.example: The program relies on partnerships with local groups.
expressions.example_cn: 这个项目依靠与本地团体的合作。
expressions.source_excerpt: This episode's partnerships have also made it possible to support Rotten Mango's team of dedicated researchers.
expressions.context_review_note: Episode partnerships suggests commercial or supporting collaborations in context, not necessarily legal partnerships or romantic partners.

expressions.definition: researchers committed to doing their work carefully and consistently
expressions.cn: 认真投入的研究人员；尽心尽责的研究人员
expressions.example: The project depends on a team of dedicated researchers.
expressions.example_cn: 项目依赖一支投入工作的研究团队。
expressions.source_excerpt: This episode's partnerships have also made it possible to support Rotten Mango's team of dedicated researchers.
expressions.context_review_note: Dedicated here praises commitment to research; the source does not establish full-time or exclusive employment. Commitment does not by itself prove that every finding is correct.

expressions.definition: insurance companies too, presented as an unexpected extreme example
expressions.example: In the story, even insurance companies refused the proposal.
expressions.example_cn: 故事中，就连保险公司也拒绝了那个提议。
expressions.source_excerpt: But there are some individuals and organizations that even insurance companies are like, we don't even want your money.
expressions.context_review_note: Even marks a surprising case on the speaker's scale, not the word evening. Source imagines companies speaking and later identifies fraternities as the example, without naming a verified quotation.

expressions.definition: committed to joining a fraternity as a prospective member
expressions.cn: 承诺加入兄弟会；成为待正式入会的新成员
expressions.example: He pledged a fraternity during his first year at college.
expressions.example_cn: 他在大学一年级时成为了一个兄弟会的待入会成员。
expressions.source_excerpt: So basically, if you're a member of a fraternity, you're 18, you went to college, you just joined a fraternity, you just pledged, you got hazed, and obviously this is vague and not directed towards one organization, but a general overview that shouldn't be taken as representative of
expressions.context_review_note: Campus-specific use of pledge, not donating money or completing full initiation. Membership procedures vary; this explains the narrator's wording only.

expressions.definition: not specific or clearly detailed
expressions.example: The schedule is still vague about the starting time.
expressions.example_cn: 日程对开始时间仍说得不够明确。
expressions.source_excerpt: So basically, if you're a member of a fraternity, you're 18, you went to college, you just joined a fraternity, you just pledged, you got hazed, and obviously this is vague and not directed towards one organization, but a general overview that shouldn't be taken as representative of
expressions.context_review_note: Here the narrator calls the overview nonspecific. Useful combinations: a vague description, vague about the details; vagueness is not proof of falsehood.

expressions.definition: aimed at or intended for a particular target
expressions.example: My feedback was directed towards the process, not the team.
expressions.example_cn: 我的反馈针对的是流程，而不是团队。
expressions.source_excerpt: So basically, if you're a member of a fraternity, you're 18, you went to college, you just joined a fraternity, you just pledged, you got hazed, and obviously this is vague and not directed towards one organization, but a general overview that shouldn't be taken as representative of
expressions.context_review_note: Not directed towards one organization denies a specific target. Towards is figurative here, not physical travel; directed at is also natural in the teaching context.

expressions.definition: typical of or accurately reflecting a wider group
expressions.cn: 能代表……的；体现……普遍情况的
expressions.example: One complaint is not necessarily representative of all customers' views.
expressions.example_cn: 一条投诉不一定能代表所有顾客的看法。
expressions.source_excerpt: So basically, if you're a member of a fraternity, you're 18, you went to college, you just joined a fraternity, you just pledged, you got hazed, and obviously this is vague and not directed towards one organization, but a general overview that shouldn't be taken as representative of
expressions.context_review_note: Shouldn't be taken as representative of means should not be interpreted as typical of. Its object continues in paragraph 195; the negative scope must be retained.

expressions.definition: was hit on the buttocks, usually as punishment
expressions.example: In the novel, the character got spanked as a child.
expressions.example_cn: 小说中的这个人物小时候被打过屁股。
expressions.source_excerpt: Yes, you got spanked.
expressions.context_review_note: Get + past participle forms a conversational passive. Here this is a concrete action in the narrator's initiation account, not figurative defeat; the teaching example describes rather than endorses it.

expressions.definition: an onion that has not been cooked
expressions.example: Would you like raw onion in your salad?
expressions.example_cn: 你的沙拉里要加生洋葱吗？
expressions.source_excerpt: You're eating an entire raw onion while being spanked, then forced to plank while professing your undying love to the brothers.
expressions.context_review_note: Raw means uncooked, not necessarily unripe; entire adds the meaning of a whole onion. The source describes coercion, unlike the voluntary food example.

expressions.definition: made to hold the body straight in a supported exercise position against one's will
expressions.example: In the story, the recruits were forced to plank as punishment.
expressions.example_cn: 故事里的新成员被迫做平板支撑作为惩罚。
expressions.source_excerpt: You're eating an entire raw onion while being spanked, then forced to plank while professing your undying love to the brothers.
expressions.context_review_note: Plank is an exercise verb here, not a wooden board. Forced to describes coercion; while being spanked and then forced compress passive actions affecting the same person.

expressions.definition: declaring that your love will never end
expressions.cn: 宣称自己永不改变的爱
expressions.example: You don't need to write a speech professing your undying love to thank someone for coffee.
expressions.example_cn: 感谢别人请你喝咖啡，不必写篇演说来宣告自己永恒的爱。
expressions.source_excerpt: You're eating an entire raw onion while being spanked, then forced to plank while professing your undying love to the brothers.
expressions.context_review_note: Profess means declare, not prove sincerity; undying is deliberately elevated or exaggerated. In the source the declaration is coerced and addressed to fraternity brothers, not literal siblings.

expressions.definition: the highest point or most impressive example of something
expressions.example: She regarded the award as the pinnacle of her career.
expressions.example_cn: 她把这个奖项看作自己职业生涯的顶峰。
expressions.source_excerpt: Weird power trip and that obviously can only mean that this is like the pinnacle of interpersonal relationships and friendship.
expressions.context_review_note: Usually praise, but here sarcastic after descriptions of coercion and a power trip. Do not present this as genuine praise of the relationships; paragraph 207 still has an unresolved transcription problem.

expressions.definition: they are expected or required to do something
expressions.cn: 他们应该……；按要求他们要……
expressions.example: They're supposed to send the agenda before the meeting.
expressions.example_cn: 按要求他们应在开会前发出议程。
expressions.source_excerpt: So it's bring your own beer and they have a whole checklist that they're supposed to do.
expressions.context_review_note: Supposed to + base verb describes an expectation, not proof of compliance. In connected speech the ending of supposed joins to to; do not interpret it as a past-tense guess.

expressions.definition: and any smaller amount or lower number
expressions.cn: 及以下；不超过所说的数量
expressions.example: The activity is for children aged ten and under.
expressions.example_cn: 这项活动面向十岁及以下的儿童。
expressions.source_excerpt: You can only bring like six beverages, like six beers and under, or like one bottle of wine.
expressions.context_review_note: Includes the stated number. Source six beers and under means up to six beers, not physical position underneath; like marks an approximate retelling, not a verified rule.

expressions.definition: a kind of something whose exact type is unspecified
expressions.example: There's some sort of problem with the connection.
expressions.example_cn: 连接似乎出了某种问题。
expressions.source_excerpt: There's some sort of limitation there.
expressions.context_review_note: Hedges the speaker's precision. Some sort of limitation does not identify the exact restriction; sort is a category noun, not the verb organize.

expressions.definition: and that is the reason that
expressions.example: The train was delayed, which is why I'm late.
expressions.example_cn: 火车晚点了，所以我迟到了。
expressions.source_excerpt: Which is why there's a lot of bad things that happen at fraternity houses.
expressions.context_review_note: Which points back to the preceding situation, not a single person. The source offers the narrator's causal explanation, not independently demonstrated causation.

expressions.definition: people in a small or closely connected circle are familiar with one another
expressions.cn: 圈子很小，大家彼此都认识
expressions.example: It's a small office where everybody knows everybody.
expressions.example_cn: 这是个小办公室，大家彼此都认识。
expressions.source_excerpt: It's like one big everybody knows everybody type of thing.
expressions.context_review_note: Informal exaggeration about connectedness, not a literal survey of every pair of people. Type of thing frames the source as an approximate description.

expressions.definition: was spent on or allocated to insurance
expressions.example: Part of our monthly budget went to insurance.
expressions.example_cn: 我们每月预算的一部分用于保险。
expressions.source_excerpt: One Redditor writes that when he was in a fraternity, quote, $50 per brother per year went to insurance, which the national office required.
expressions.context_review_note: Money goes to + purpose/recipient. Per brother per year sets a per-person annual rate; source is an attributed Reddit account, not a verified fee schedule.

expressions.definition: the important point or difficulty is what follows
expressions.example: The thing is, we don't have enough chairs for everyone.
expressions.example_cn: 问题是，我们没有足够的椅子让每个人都坐下。
expressions.source_excerpt: The thing is, if you read the insurance policy, anything that could result in a chapter or national organization being sued was either a violation of fraternity bylaws or the insurance policy itself, in which case no coverage is offered.
expressions.context_review_note: Discourse opener introducing a complication; not a reference to a physical object. A short pause after is is natural, but no exact audio realization is claimed.

expressions.definition: an entire interconnected world or network, used figuratively here
expressions.cn: 一整个相互关联的圈子或体系
expressions.example: The article describes a whole ecosphere of small businesses around the station.
expressions.example_cn: 文章描述了车站周边由小企业组成的一整个相互关联的商业圈。
expressions.source_excerpt: It's like a whole ecosphere of lawyers who only take on fraternity cases.
expressions.context_review_note: Figurative extension of an ecological term; ecosystem is a more usual business metaphor. Source describes a specialized legal circle, not a biological environment.

expressions.definition: hit forcefully in the head
expressions.example: In the story, he was rammed in the head by a falling box.
expressions.example_cn: 故事里，他的头被掉下来的箱子猛地砸中。
expressions.source_excerpt: But also, if you're with a bunch of fraternity brothers throwing a football around and then you get rammed in the head with a football in the front yard as a full pledged brother, well, according to the Redditor, quote, insurance does not cover brothers who sue the chapter or national organization for any reason as they are considered the same party on the same plan.
expressions.context_review_note: Get rammed is passive; in the head identifies the affected body part. Source describes a hypothetical football impact; it does not establish an actual injury or insurance outcome.

expressions.definition: cannot bring a court action against them as well, in the speaker's stated conclusion
expressions.cn: 也不能起诉他们（说话人的推断）
expressions.example: In the fictional dispute, she says, 'You can't sue them either,' but gives no reason.
expressions.example_cn: 在这个虚构的纠纷中，她说“你也不能起诉他们”，却没有说明理由。
expressions.source_excerpt: So you can't sue them either.
expressions.context_review_note: Either at the end adds a negative alternative; it does not mean choose between two. The source's conclusion does not follow merely from an insurance exclusion. This is language interpretation, not a legal restriction.

expressions.definition: selected a smaller set from a larger group to examine
expressions.cn: 抽取了一部分……作为样本
expressions.example: We took a sample of customer comments to discuss at the meeting.
expressions.example_cn: 我们抽取了一部分顾客评论，准备在会上讨论。
expressions.source_excerpt: According to one insurance company who does insure fraternities, they took a sample of liability claims and they analyzed what kind of claims they were.
expressions.context_review_note: Sample is a subset, not necessarily a representative one. Does insure emphasizes that the company actually offers insurance; claims are grouped, not independently proven by sampling.

expressions.definition: making or arranging for their prospective members to perform an action
expressions.example: The club was having its new members introduce themselves.
expressions.example_cn: 俱乐部正在让新成员做自我介绍。
expressions.source_excerpt: But in a very rather uncomfortable turn of events, I guess you could say, they discovered that the fraternity was actually having, well, allegedly, having their new pledges stick plastic hoses up their butts to give themselves enemas
expressions.context_review_note: Causative have + person + base verb: source continues with stick, not to stick. The speaker inserts allegedly to qualify the account. The benign teaching example illustrates grammar, not the source's harmful act.

expressions.definition: flexible plastic tubes used to carry liquid or gas
expressions.example: The shop sells plastic hoses for watering gardens.
expressions.example_cn: 这家店出售浇灌花园用的塑料软管。
expressions.source_excerpt: But in a very rather uncomfortable turn of events, I guess you could say, they discovered that the fraternity was actually having, well, allegedly, having their new pledges stick plastic hoses up their butts to give themselves enemas
expressions.context_review_note: Hose is a flexible tube, not house. Source stick ... up describes insertion into the body and butts means buttocks; this is receptive vocabulary only, not a procedure to imitate.

expressions.definition: became unable to control the passing of stool
expressions.cn: 大便失禁；无法控制排便
expressions.example: The character was embarrassed after he lost control of his bowels.
expressions.example_cn: 这个人物大便失禁后感到难堪。
expressions.source_excerpt: However police found circumstantial evidence in the fraternity house including evidence that the patient may have lost control of his bowels in the process and defecated on himself which he also has no recollection of
expressions.context_review_note: Bowels means the intestines, not bowls. May have lost marks a tentative inference in the source, not a diagnosis; the card explains the phrase without establishing what happened.

expressions.definition: passed stool onto his own body or clothing
expressions.cn: 排便弄脏了自己或自己的衣物
expressions.example: The report said the patient had defecated on himself.
expressions.example_cn: 报告称那位病人排便弄脏了自己。
expressions.source_excerpt: However police found circumstantial evidence in the fraternity house including evidence that the patient may have lost control of his bowels in the process and defecated on himself which he also has no recollection of
expressions.context_review_note: Defecate is formal for pass stool; on himself describes where it ended up. The source links this to circumstantial evidence and reported lack of memory, neither of which is proof by itself.

expressions.definition: looking alert and enthusiastic
expressions.cn: 神采奕奕的；充满热情的
expressions.example: A bright-eyed student arrived early for the workshop.
expressions.example_cn: 一位精神饱满的学生早早来参加工作坊。
expressions.source_excerpt: Bright-eyed college student ends up in the er wine enema allegedly so
expressions.context_review_note: Usually positive; here it contributes to the narrator's ironic headline-like remark after injury. Keep the source fragment separate from the grammatical teaching example.

expressions.definition: emergency room, the hospital department for urgent treatment
expressions.example: He waited in the ER while his friend was being examined.
expressions.example_cn: 朋友接受检查时，他在急诊室等候。
expressions.source_excerpt: Bright-eyed college student ends up in the er wine enema allegedly so
expressions.context_review_note: Read the letters E-R in American English; source lowercase er is retained as the literal target, while standard teaching spelling is ER. The surrounding broken syntax remains unverified.

expressions.definition: hitting someone with a flat board, here as punishment
expressions.cn: 用扁平木板打人（此处指打屁股）
expressions.example: The novel describes paddling as a form of punishment.
expressions.example_cn: 小说把用木板打人描写为一种惩罚。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now they need new skin or paddling gone wrong, causing permanent aesthetic and emotional damage to one's bottom.
expressions.context_review_note: Not rowing or splashing in shallow water here. The same object is named paddles in 271; the source is describing harm, not recommending discipline.

expressions.definition: relating to appearance or how something looks
expressions.example: The scratch caused aesthetic damage but did not affect the table's stability.
expressions.example_cn: 划痕影响了桌子的外观，但没有影响稳固性。
expressions.source_excerpt: Now they need new skin or paddling gone wrong, causing permanent aesthetic and emotional damage to one's bottom.
expressions.context_review_note: Source contrasts appearance with emotional damage; bottom means buttocks here, not a financial result. Do not confuse aesthetic with anesthetic.

expressions.definition: pass urine from the body
expressions.example: The sign asks visitors not to urinate in the alley.
expressions.example_cn: 告示要求访客不要在巷子里小便。
expressions.source_excerpt: They fall out of open windows while trying to urinate out the window when they're intoxicated.
expressions.context_review_note: Formal verb corresponding to everyday pee. Out the window indicates direction through an opening; while trying to shares the subject with fall. The source depicts dangerous conduct, not advice.

expressions.definition: appear to resist the normal downward pull of gravity
expressions.cn: 仿佛违背重力；看起来能腾空或倒立不倒
expressions.example: The dancer seemed to defy gravity during the leap.
expressions.example_cn: 舞者跳跃时仿佛摆脱了重力。
expressions.source_excerpt: The promise of being able to defy gravity and do a keg stand on a random Thursday night.
expressions.context_review_note: Often figurative or hyperbolic, not a claim of violating physics. Here the expression connects to the upside-down drinking stunt mentioned next.

expressions.definition: a drinking stunt involving an upside-down position at a beer keg
expressions.cn: 倒立喝桶装啤酒的酒局花样
expressions.example: She refused to take part in a keg stand.
expressions.example_cn: 她拒绝参加倒立喝啤酒的活动。
expressions.source_excerpt: The promise of being able to defy gravity and do a keg stand on a random Thursday night.
expressions.context_review_note: Receptive cultural term, not a furniture stand. No steps or quantities are supplied. Random Thursday night means an ordinary, unplanned weekday evening, adding to the narrator's party-life contrast.

expressions.definition: that does not mean or imply
expressions.cn: 这并不意味着……；这不是说……
expressions.example: The price is low, but that's not saying the quality is poor.
expressions.example_cn: 价格低，但这并不意味着质量差。
expressions.source_excerpt: And that's not saying that there aren't a lot of hazing lawsuits.
expressions.context_review_note: Rejects an inference. Source not saying + there aren't a lot denies the inference that there are few hazing lawsuits; it does not deny their existence.

expressions.definition: allow someone to enter an institution as a student
expressions.example: The program plans to admit more students next year.
expressions.example_cn: 这个项目计划明年录取更多学生。
expressions.source_excerpt: It also allows institutions to expand the number of students they can admit, which means more tuition.
expressions.context_review_note: Educational sense here, not confess a wrongdoing. Allows + object + to expand describes an enabled increase, and more tuition means more fee revenue in the narrator's argument.

expressions.definition: thrown onto a large piece of cloth, here apparently a bedsheet
expressions.cn: 被抛到一块布单上（这里看来指床单）
expressions.example: In the novel, the clothes were tossed onto a sheet on the floor.
expressions.example_cn: 小说里，衣服被扔到地板上的一块布单上。
expressions.source_excerpt: He alleges that he's sleep deprived, physically exhausted, and quote, I was blindfolded and tossed onto a sheet, flinging me up and down.
expressions.context_review_note: Toss is throw; onto marks movement to a surface. A sheet is cloth in this scene, not a sheet of paper. Blindfolded and tossed share the passive I was in the quoted account.

expressions.definition: throwing or moving me forcefully upward and downward repeatedly
expressions.example: In the story, the giant shouted, 'Stop flinging me up and down!'
expressions.example_cn: 故事里，巨人大喊：“别再把我上下抛来抛去了！”
expressions.source_excerpt: He alleges that he's sleep deprived, physically exhausted, and quote, I was blindfolded and tossed onto a sheet, flinging me up and down.
expressions.context_review_note: Fling is a forceful throw. Me identifies the affected person; the participial phrase describes the repeated movement rather than a voluntary jump. No exact gesture or method is reconstructed.

expressions.definition: spread a thick or generous layer of something over a surface
expressions.example: She slathered butter on the toast.
expressions.example_cn: 她在吐司上涂了厚厚的黄油。
expressions.source_excerpt: Hands reached under the waistband of my basketball shorts and slathered fistfuls of spicy mung all over my genitals.
expressions.context_review_note: Slather something on/over something; the generous amount distinguishes it from a light smear. Source describes alleged nonconsensual contact; the food example is an unrelated teaching illustration.

expressions.definition: amounts that can be held in a closed hand
expressions.example: He scattered fistfuls of seeds over the soil.
expressions.example_cn: 他把一把把种子撒在土上。
expressions.source_excerpt: Hands reached under the waistband of my basketball shorts and slathered fistfuls of spicy mung all over my genitals.
expressions.context_review_note: Fist + -ful names an approximate handful-sized quantity, not a punch. The plural means repeated amounts, not a precise measurement.

expressions.definition: the external sexual organs
expressions.example: The textbook uses the neutral anatomical term genitals.
expressions.example_cn: 教科书使用了“外生殖器”这一中性的解剖学用语。
expressions.source_excerpt: Hands reached under the waistband of my basketball shorts and slathered fistfuls of spicy mung all over my genitals.
expressions.context_review_note: Plural anatomical noun, more formal than junk in paragraph 350. The source explicitly alleges unwanted contact; naming the body part does not supply consent.

expressions.definition: a food made from oats, often cooked into a porridge
expressions.cn: 燕麦食品；这里指燕麦粥
expressions.example: I had oatmeal and fruit for breakfast.
expressions.example_cn: 我早餐吃了燕麦粥和水果。
expressions.source_excerpt: He says mung consisted of cold oatmeal, vinegar, hot sauce, and cayenne pepper.
expressions.context_review_note: American food sense; cold describes its temperature in the source. Mung is the speaker's name for the described mixture, not a claim that it contains mung beans or a standardized food name.

expressions.definition: spread over a surface, often unevenly
expressions.example: Paint was smeared across the table.
expressions.example_cn: 油漆被抹得桌上到处都是。
expressions.source_excerpt: Smeared all over his genitals but he did not consent to anyone touching him or inflicting this amount of pain he says i screamed bloody murder
expressions.context_review_note: Source is a passive fragment continuing the previous mixture description. Smeared is physical here, not the figurative reputational attack in smear someone's name.

expressions.definition: agree to anyone making physical contact with him
expressions.example: He did not consent to anyone touching him during the demonstration.
expressions.example_cn: 他没有同意任何人在演示中触碰他。
expressions.source_excerpt: Smeared all over his genitals but he did not consent to anyone touching him or inflicting this amount of pain he says i screamed bloody murder
expressions.context_review_note: Consent to + noun/-ing; to is a preposition, not an infinitive marker here. The source explicitly negates consent, and or inflicting continues the scope of that negation.

expressions.definition: half of the volume called a gallon
expressions.example: We bought a half gallon of milk.
expressions.example_cn: 我们买了半加仑牛奶。
expressions.source_excerpt: A few minutes later i was given a half gallon of milk to wash off my spicy junk
expressions.context_review_note: An American volume expression; not half a bottle of unspecified size. The amount in the account is not a recommendation for treating pain or injury.

expressions.definition: an informal, sometimes crude term for male genitals in this context
expressions.cn: 男性生殖器（粗俗口语，此处不是垃圾）
expressions.example: The dialogue uses junk as slang for a man's genitals.
expressions.example_cn: 这段对话用 junk 这个俚语指男性生殖器。
expressions.source_excerpt: A few minutes later i was given a half gallon of milk to wash off my spicy junk
expressions.context_review_note: Common everyday junk means unwanted stuff; here my spicy junk refers to the affected body area. Wash off names removal, not an endorsed medical treatment.

expressions.definition: well known for something bad
expressions.cn: 臭名昭著的；因坏事出名的
expressions.example: The road is infamous for its traffic jams.
expressions.example_cn: 这条路因经常堵车而出名。
expressions.source_excerpt: He says he was initiated and he starts living at the now infamous Kai-Fi house at Cornell.
expressions.context_review_note: Unlike famous, carries a negative evaluation. The source's now is relative to the narration; this vocabulary note does not independently establish reputation or correct the Kai-Fi spelling.

expressions.definition: a fraternity-themed wordplay on the title The Great Gatsby
expressions.cn: 把《了不起的盖茨比》与 frat（兄弟会）结合的派对名称双关
expressions.example: The invitation called it a Great Fratsby party, a pun on The Great Gatsby.
expressions.example_cn: 邀请函把它称为“Great Fratsby”派对，借《了不起的盖茨比》的书名玩了个双关。
expressions.source_excerpt: We had a great Fratsby party.
expressions.context_review_note: Frat is informal for fraternity; Fratsby is a coined name, not a normal adjective or a general idiom. The title allusion does not establish the actual party's decorations or activities.

expressions.definition: organizing or hosting a party or similar event
expressions.example: We're throwing a small party for her graduation.
expressions.example_cn: 我们要为她毕业办一个小聚会。
expressions.source_excerpt: We're not kicking people out, but we're just going to investigate and you guys lose your privileges of throwing fucking ragers and doing keg stands.
expressions.context_review_note: Throw a party is host it, not physically throw an object. Source combines throwing with ragers and an intensifying swear word; the neutral example does not promote excessive drinking.

expressions.definition: large, wild parties, often involving heavy drinking, in slang
expressions.cn: 喧闹狂欢的派对（常涉及大量饮酒，俚语）
expressions.example: He prefers quiet dinners to ragers.
expressions.example_cn: 比起狂欢派对，他更喜欢安静地吃顿饭。
expressions.source_excerpt: We're not kicking people out, but we're just going to investigate and you guys lose your privileges of throwing fucking ragers and doing keg stands.
expressions.context_review_note: Party sense here, not angry people. The word is informal; source discusses withdrawing party privileges, not an invitation to attend.

expressions.definition: promotes or praises itself enthusiastically
expressions.cn: 大力宣扬自己；自我标榜
expressions.example: The cafe touts itself as the quietest place on the street.
expressions.example_cn: 这家咖啡馆自称是这条街上最安静的地方。
expressions.source_excerpt: The same Chi Phi, the fraternity that touts itself, their whole mission, their motto is building better men.
expressions.context_review_note: Tout itself as + description; advertising claim is not independent evidence. The source contrasts the organization's self-presentation with allegations.

expressions.definition: a short phrase expressing a group's guiding ideal
expressions.cn: 格言；座右铭；组织的理念口号
expressions.example: Our team's motto is 'Keep it simple.'
expressions.example_cn: 我们团队的座右铭是“保持简单”。
expressions.source_excerpt: The same Chi Phi, the fraternity that touts itself, their whole mission, their motto is building better men.
expressions.context_review_note: Motto is a stated ideal, not proof of behavior. Source building better men is presented as the organization's slogan, not the course's endorsement.

expressions.text: the hand of brotherhood is always extended
